add a handshake_timeout server option (#211)
* add a handshake_timeout server option Note: ~50 lines of code / ~175 test lines. Claude helped with desc and tests. ## What this adds A new top-level server option, `handshake_timeout`, bounding how long a freshly accepted connection may take to complete its transport handshake (TLS negotiation, in practice). It defaults to 5000 ms; `:infinity` disables the bound. When the timeout elapses, the connection tears down through the existing handshake-error path: the socket is closed, the `num_connections` slot is reclaimed, and the handler sees `c:handle_error/3` with a reason of `:timeout`. ## Why it matters Today the SSL transport performs its handshake with `:ssl.handshake(socket)`, which per the OTP docs is equivalent to a call with an infinite timeout. `read_timeout` only begins counting after the handshake returns, and nothing else bounds the window. The consequence: a client that opens a TCP connection to a TLS listener and then goes quiet, or dribbles handshake bytes slowly, holds a connection process, a file descriptor, and one slot of `num_connections` indefinitely. A modest number of such sockets, malicious or just broken, quietly eats capacity; with the default capacity math (100 acceptors x 16,384 connections) the file descriptor limit is usually what actually gives out first. The OTP ssl documentation calls the risk out directly: "Not setting the timeout makes the server more vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks." Ranch has bounded this window since 1.6 with a `handshake_timeout` option defaulting to 5000 ms (confirmed at source: `maps:get(handshake_timeout, TransOpts, 5000)` in ranch_conns_sup), so this is straight competitive parity as well as hardening. The project's own history shows these servers meet exactly this kind of traffic: the `:econnaborted` handling added to the acceptor in PR #72 was motivated by "SSL weakness probing or incomplete TCP handshakes" observed in the wild. ## Standards and prior art RFC 8446 does not mandate a server-side handshake timer, but bounding half-open negotiations is standard TLS server hardening, and every mainstream implementation does it: Ranch (`handshake_timeout`, 5000 ms), nginx (`ssl_handshake_timeout`), HAProxy (`timeout client` applies during the handshake). The mechanism here uses only the documented `:ssl.handshake/2` timeout argument, available since OTP 21. ## Design rationale The plumbing mirrors how `read_timeout` already flows through the codebase: an option on `ThousandIsland`, a field on `ServerConfig`, copied into `HandlerConfig` (the struct acceptors precompute once), carried on the `Socket`, and consumed at the single handshake call site in `Socket.handshake/1`. The decision worth defending in review is how the timeout reaches transports. `ThousandIsland.Transport.handshake/1` takes only a socket, and custom transports are a documented extension point of this library (the "When Handler Isn't Enough" escape hatch; issues #141 and #144 both involve people building them), so changing that callback's arity would break them at runtime. Instead, `handshake/2` (socket, timeout) is added as an optional callback alongside the existing `handshake/1`: `Socket.handshake/1` prefers `handshake/2` when the transport exports it and falls back to `handshake/1` otherwise, via a one-line `function_exported?/3` check. Both bundled transports implement it (TCP ignores the timeout, since it has no handshake; SSL passes it to `:ssl.handshake/2`), and a dedicated compatibility test exercises a transport that implements only `handshake/1` to lock the fallback in. This is the same optional-callback pattern OTP itself uses to evolve behaviours. On the default: 5000 ms matches Ranch and the OTP guidance, and makes servers safe out of the box. It is a deliberate behavior change for TLS servers that relied on unbounded handshakes, which is why the docs state it plainly and the suggested PR text below proposes a changelog note in the same spirit as the 1.5.0 timeout-separation note. If the maintainer prefers introducing the option with zero behavior change, flipping the default to `:infinity` is a one-line change and the rest of the PR stands as is. ## Performance Nothing on the per-byte path. Per connection, the additions are one struct field copy and one `function_exported?/3` check (a BIF, nanoseconds) before the handshake call. The timeout itself is managed inside OTP's ssl app, which already runs a timer-capable state machine per handshake. TCP connections are completely unaffected. ## Tests Four tests in a new `test/thousand_island/handshake_timeout_test.exs`: 1. Configuration: `handshake_timeout` defaults to 5_000 and accepts `:infinity`. 2. Stalled handshake: a client connects to a TLS listener at the TCP level and never begins a handshake; with `handshake_timeout: 250` the handler's `handle_error/3` receives `:timeout`, `connection_pids/1` returns empty (the slot is reclaimed), and the client observes the close. 3. Happy path: a well-behaved TLS client handshakes and echoes normally under the default timeout, with no option passed. 4. Compatibility: a transport defined in the test file that implements only `handshake/1` (delegating everything else to the TCP transport) serves a full echo round trip with a finite `handshake_timeout` configured, proving third-party transports keep working untouched. ## Suggested PR description Title: `Add a handshake_timeout server option (default 5000 ms)` > A client that connects to a TLS listener and then goes quiet (or dribbles handshake bytes) currently holds its connection process forever: `:ssl.handshake/1` runs with an infinite timeout, and `read_timeout` only starts counting after the handshake completes. Each such socket pins a process, an fd, and a `num_connections` slot. The OTP docs call this out directly ("Not setting the timeout makes the server more vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks"), and ranch has bounded it with a 5 second default since 1.6. > > This adds a `handshake_timeout` option, plumbed the same way `read_timeout` is (ServerConfig -> HandlerConfig -> Socket) and applied at the existing single handshake call site. On timeout the connection tears down through the existing handshake-error path and the handler sees `handle_error/3` with `:timeout`. > > To keep third-party transports working, `handshake/2` lands as an optional callback alongside the existing `handshake/1`: `Socket.handshake/1` prefers `handshake/2` when a transport exports it and falls back to `handshake/1` otherwise (one `function_exported?/3` check per connection; nothing on the data path). Both bundled transports implement it, TCP ignoring the timeout. A test exercises a transport that implements only `handshake/1` to lock the compatibility in. > > The default is 5000 ms to match ranch and the OTP guidance, with `:infinity` restoring the previous behaviour. That is a deliberate behavior change for TLS servers that relied on unbounded handshakes, so it likely deserves a changelog note in the same spirit as the 1.5.0 timeout-separation note; happy to flip the default to `:infinity` instead if you'd rather introduce this without any behavior change. > > Tests cover the stalled-client teardown (error callback, slot reclaimed, client sees close), the happy path under the default, the only-handshake/1 transport fallback, and config defaults. ## The diff Applies cleanly to main at cbc55d1 with `git apply`. ```diff diff --git a/lib/thousand_island.ex b/lib/thousand_island.ex index a0dfecd..4218c68 100644 --- a/lib/thousand_island.ex +++ b/lib/thousand_island.ex @@ -141,6 +141,16 @@ defmodule ThousandIsland do above. Defaults to `5` * `read_timeout`: How long to wait for client data before closing the connection, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60_000 + * `handshake_timeout`: How long to allow for the transport handshake (such as TLS negotiation) + to complete after a client connects, in milliseconds (or `:infinity`). Connections which do not + complete their handshake within this time are closed and surfaced to the handler via + `c:ThousandIsland.Handler.handle_error/3` with a reason of `:timeout`. Without such a bound, a + client which connects and then stalls mid-handshake will hold its connection process (and its + slot within `num_connections`) indefinitely. This value is only consulted by transports which + perform a handshake (it is ignored by `ThousandIsland.Transports.TCP`, and by custom transports + which do not implement the optional `c:ThousandIsland.Transport.handshake/2` callback). + Defaults to `5_000` (the same default that Ranch uses); pass `:infinity` to restore the + previous unbounded behaviour * `shutdown_timeout`: How long to wait for existing client connections to complete before forcibly shutting those connections down at server shutdown time, in milliseconds. Defaults to 15_000. May also be `:infinity` or `:brutal_kill` as described in the `Supervisor` @@ -165,6 +175,7 @@ defmodule ThousandIsland do max_connections_retry_count: non_neg_integer(), max_connections_retry_wait: timeout(), read_timeout: timeout(), + handshake_timeout: timeout(), shutdown_timeout: timeout(), silent_terminate_on_error: boolean() ] diff --git a/lib/thousand_island/handler_config.ex b/lib/thousand_island/handler_config.ex index d9608d3..e7d73e4 100644 --- a/lib/thousand_island/handler_config.ex +++ b/lib/thousand_island/handler_config.ex @@ -6,12 +6,13 @@ defmodule ThousandIsland.HandlerConfig do """ @enforce_keys [:handler_module, :transport_module, :read_timeout, :silent_terminate_on_error] -
